elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate
elements.evidence: "M&I's consent need not be obtained in connection with the assignment of this Agreement to an Affiliate of Customer"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or pursuant to a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of the assets, stock or securities of Customer"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's prior consent
elements.evidence: "M&I may assign this Agreement only with Customer's prior written consent"

elements.element: That Customer consent is not to be unreasonably withheld
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of Customer"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "If a Change in Control occurs with respect to Customer, M&I agrees to continue to provide Services under this Agreement" — no termination right is conferred

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Vendor successor assignment is now consent-gated: "M&I may assign this Agreement only with Customer's prior written consent"
No notice mechanic appears; carve-out (a) is conditioned only on "the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present: Customer affiliate and successor (merger/acquisition/substantially-all-assets) assignment free of Vendor consent, Vendor assignment gated by Customer's consent not unreasonably withheld, an absolute competitor bar, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control (Section B affirmatively requires continued Services).

Edits are confined to the two operative carve-outs; the mutual consent lead-in, the Section 21.11 condition, and Vendor's (i)/(ii) transaction descriptions are left intact, so no more was changed than needed.

Fallback is independently incomplete (no written-notice mechanic and Vendor's successor assignment is no longer a free right), but that is immaterial because the locked target is preferred and it is fully met.

Note in the rationale only: the pre-existing change-of-control volume limitation (accounts/items plus 25%) and the Section 21.11 conditions remain untouched; these are existing commercial terms, not new deviations.
